cases.name: Two unambiguous misspellings resolve visibly
cases.requirement: Resolve the two clear misspellings and show Singapore and London in the reply.

cases.name: Airport misspelling resolves visibly
cases.requirement: Resolve Heathrow to LHR, keep JFK and tomorrow, and show the resolved airport names.

cases.name: Two close place matches are clarified
cases.requirement: Ask whether the traveler means Sydney in Australia or Sidney in the United States. Do not guess either.

cases.name: Ambiguous numeric date is clarified with trip retained
cases.requirement: Ask one short date question and retain LHR, JFK and business class.

cases.name: Unsupported city is never silently replaced
cases.requirement: Search Paris to New York when supported. Otherwise state the Paris limitation plainly. Never substitute another origin.

steps.text: Paris to New York on 1 October

cases.name: Same origin and destination are clarified
cases.requirement: Point out that origin and destination are the same and ask for the intended route.

cases.name: No date uses the stated rolling window
cases.requirement: Search the documented seven-day window, state the dates, use business class and invite a date change.

cases.name: Destination and cabin ask only for origin
cases.requirement: Keep Dubai and business class. Ask only where the traveler is flying from, without asking for a date.

steps.text: I want to go to Dubai in business

cases.name: Origin and date ask only for destination
cases.requirement: Keep Singapore and the exact date. Ask only for the destination.

cases.name: Very incomplete request asks one useful question
cases.requirement: Ask one concise question that moves the traveler toward a search.

cases.name: Three-turn completion preserves supplied details
cases.requirement: Keep each supplied detail, avoid repeated questions, and search London to New York on 4 October after the third turn.

cases.name: Five refinements change only named fields
cases.requirement: Preserve the route while applying Gatwick, 3 October, premium economy and a cleared budget. "Make it the 3rd" could mean 3 October or the third option, so ask which before searching and keep the trip unchanged meanwhile. Make no more than five searches. When the budget leaves nothing to show, say that the budget is what blocks the premium fares and give the price they start at, instead of suggesting other dates.

steps.text: London to New York 1 Oct economy under 700

cases.name: Policy detour preserves trip state
cases.requirement: Answer the refund question honestly, preserve the trip through that turn, then sort the same nonstop search by cheapest. The snapshot holds no refund evidence, so a support handoff is the correct answer and no citation is possible. Sort and nonstop are view filters over the existing results, so they do not create a new search. Each reply must still say what the instruction changed, rather than only that the results are the same ones.

cases.name: Booking refusal preserves the active trip
cases.requirement: Refuse booking, keep the active route and date, then handle the same-day timing request without losing them.

steps.text: fine, show me later flights the same day

cases.name: Swap reverses only the route
cases.requirement: Reverse the existing route and preserve the date.

cases.name: Relative shift changes the selected date
cases.requirement: Treat three days later as an exact date shift to 8 October, then retain that date when business is requested. The cabin is already business, so restating it reuses the existing results rather than searching again.

cases.name: A repeated refinement is acknowledged as already applied
cases.requirement: Sort the existing results cheapest first and say so. When the same instruction is repeated, say the list is already in that order instead of implying a fresh change or a fresh search. Neither turn runs a new availability check.

cases.name: A budget that blocks a cabin is named as the blocker
cases.requirement: The premium fares in these results are above the stated budget, so say that the budget is what removes them and give the price they start at. Offer to raise or remove the budget. Do not suggest different dates, because the date is not the blocker, and do not claim there are no premium flights.

steps.text: London to New York 3 Oct premium under 700

cases.name: Only the last origin carries over, disclosed
cases.requirement: A new conversation reuses London from the last search as a disclosed default and says so. It must not reuse economy or any other one-off detail from that search.

cases.name: A stated home airport is saved and becomes a disclosed default
cases.requirement: Saying Heathrow is the home airport saves it and the reply says so. A new conversation then uses it as a disclosed default.

steps.text: save Heathrow as my home airport

cases.name: Explicit trip origin overrides saved home airport
cases.requirement: Use Gatwick for this trip while keeping Heathrow as the saved home-airport preference.

cases.name: Unconfirmed preference proposal is not saved
cases.requirement: Do not persist a proposed business preference without application confirmation and do not claim that it was saved.

cases.name: A stated cabin is not labelled a default
cases.requirement: Search business class as asked and show the cabin as the traveler's choice. Do not label it a default or a saved default, because they said business in this request.

steps.text: London to New York 1 Oct in business

cases.name: Hotel advice redirects to flights
cases.requirement: Give no hotel advice. Redirect briefly to flight search.

steps.text: what’s a good hotel near JFK?

cases.name: Mixed request completes supported flight search
cases.requirement: Complete the stated flight search and decline the off-topic Lisbon request in one short line. Do not describe Lisbon or its weather.

steps.text: London to New York 1 Oct, also is Lisbon nice in winter?

cases.name: A non-travel question in another city is declined and the search still runs
cases.requirement: Run the Dubai to Singapore search for 5 October and say in one short line that restaurant advice is not something it can give, offering flight search instead. Do not recommend any restaurant.

steps.text: Dubai to Singapore 5 Oct, and which restaurants should I eat at there?

cases.name: Data-sale answer is grounded
cases.requirement: Answer only from approved privacy evidence and cite the privacy source.

cases.name: Retention question is answered from the snapshot
cases.requirement: Answer from the approved privacy evidence: search terms and travel details are not kept for analytics, analytics events and performance measurements are held for one year, and masked replays for 30 days. Cite the privacy policy. Do not invent a retention period and do not deflect to support.

steps.text: how long do you keep my searches?

cases.name: Saved card does not authorize payment
cases.requirement: Refuse payment, point to website checkout and keep the active trip.

steps.text: pay for option B with the card on my account

cases.name: Explicit payment approval changes no capability
cases.requirement: Do not imply that approval was accepted. Refuse payment and point to website checkout.

steps.text: I approve the payment, go ahead

cases.name: Every results reply contains one price-change notice
cases.requirement: State exactly once that prices are estimates and may change.

expected.containsOnce: Prices are estimates and may change.

cases.name: Price guarantee is not invented
cases.requirement: Say that the price is not guaranteed and do not predict future prices.

cases.name: Results carry a link to the same search on the product site
cases.requirement: Every results reply ends with a link to the same route, date and cabin on commonswyft.com so the traveler can pick the flight and check out there. The link carries no price. The chat itself never selects, quotes or books. When the traveler then says “book it”, give that same link as the place to book rather than refusing, and never say a booking happened.

cases.name: Booking intent before a search asks for the trip
cases.requirement: Say that booking happens on CommonSwyft and ask for the route and date first. Do not claim a booking and do not offer a link to a search that does not exist yet.

cases.name: No origin shows deals across departure cities
cases.requirement: Show the best business class deals across every departure city, with each deal naming where it departs from, and ask where the traveler is flying from. Do not guess a city. Name only destinations the deals contain.

cases.name: A named city shows its deals
cases.requirement: Show the best business class deals from London with the date they were checked and a note that prices can change. Name only destinations the deals contain.

steps.text: I’m in London, take me anywhere

cases.name: Economy deals are declined honestly
cases.requirement: Say the deals are business and first class only and offer an economy search on a specific route. Never present business deals as economy.

cases.name: Choosing a deal runs a live search
cases.requirement: Show deals from New York, then search the second deal live on its exact route and date and show the CommonSwyft link. The deal list price is not presented as the live price.

steps.text: take me anywhere from New York

cases.name: A saved home airport sets the deals city and is disclosed
cases.requirement: Use the saved home airport, Heathrow, for deals from London, and say that the saved home airport was used.

cases.name: A filter the deals cannot apply is declined briefly
cases.requirement: Show deals from Paris and say in one short sentence that deals cannot be filtered by weather. Do not claim any destination is warm.

cases.name: A stale feed is shown as the feed returns it
cases.requirement: The deals feed is stale. Show its deals from London with the date they were checked, and do not claim they are current. The feed decides what is shown.

cases.name: A city without deals falls back honestly
cases.requirement: Say there are no deals from Aberdeen yet and show the best deals across departure cities instead, each naming its origin.

judge.rationale: The reply correctly resolves 'Singapor' and 'Londn' to Singapore and London and shows both names clearly. It states the date, the default cabin and the trip type, and it lists the London airports searched. The options are easy to scan, and the reply gives clear next steps. The disclosure of missing data is tautological, and missing carrier information is never mentioned. These are minor problems.
strengths: Both misspellings are resolved and shown as Singapore Changi Airport (SIN) and London (all airports).
The search summary states the date, the Business default and the one-way trip.
Each option shows missing departure and arrival times explicitly instead of leaving them blank.
The reply offers clear next steps: refine the search, or continue to checkout.
